scenes.title: Replication & In-Sync Replicas
scenes.subtitle: How Kafka survives broker failures
scenes.narration: Replication copies each partition across brokers, and the in-sync replica set determines how durable those copies really are.

scenes.title: The Replication Model
bullets: Each partition has one leader and several followers
Producers and consumers talk only to the leader
Followers continuously fetch from the leader
Replication factor sets the number of copies
scenes.narration: Every partition has exactly one leader replica and zero or more follower replicas. Producers write to and consumers read from the leader only. Followers continuously fetch new records from the leader to stay current. The replication factor, set when you create the topic, determines how many total copies exist across the brokers.

scenes.title: Staying In Sync
steps: Leader fails, ISR member takes over
scenes.narration: When the leader receives a write, followers fetch that record as quickly as they can. Followers that stay caught up within a time bound belong to the in-sync replica set, or ISR. If the leader fails, Kafka promotes a member of the ISR to be the new leader. This guarantees the new leader already holds all committed data.

scenes.title: Durability Trade-offs

left.heading: min.insync.replicas=1
points: Writes succeed with just the leader

scenes.narration: The min.insync.replicas setting controls durability alongside acks. Setting it to one lets writes succeed with only the leader, favoring availability but risking loss. Setting it to two, combined with acks all, requires at least two in-sync copies before a write is acknowledged. If the ISR shrinks below that threshold, Kafka rejects new writes rather than risk losing data.

scenes.title: Enforcing Durability
scenes.code:
# Require 2 in-sync replicas on a topic
kafka-configs.sh --alter \
  --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 \
  --entity-type topics --entity-name payments \
  --add-config min.insync.replicas=2

# Producer must then use acks=all
scenes.narration: This command sets min.insync.replicas to two on the payments topic. Combined with a producer using acks all, Kafka now requires at least two in-sync replicas to confirm each write. If only the leader remains available, writes fail fast instead of silently accepting data that could be lost. This is the standard configuration for financial and other critical streams.

scenes.text: Use replication factor 3 with min.insync.replicas=2 and acks=all for the durability sweet spot: survive one broker loss with no data loss.
scenes.narration: As a best practice, use a replication factor of three with min.insync.replicas of two and acks all. This is the durability sweet spot, letting you survive one broker failure with no data loss.
